paragraphs: Two layers, from examples/26. The REST client's read timeout in application.properties bounds every call to the backend at 2 seconds. The deadline endpoint subtracts the edge's overhead from the caller's budget, refuses at once when too little remains, and otherwise builds a client whose read timeout is the remaining budget and sends that number in the X-Deadline-Ms header, so the backend can refuse work it cannot finish.

paragraphs: SmallRye Fault Tolerance, the MicroProfile implementation in Quarkus. @Retry sets two retries after the first attempt, a 100 ms delay with up to 50 ms of jitter, and the exceptions that count; @ExponentialBackoff doubles the delay up to 2 seconds. The annotations are CDI interceptors, so they only apply when another bean calls the method, which is why the example keeps them on a Backend bean that the REST resource calls. Retry only idempotent calls, and pair the retry with a circuit breaker.

paragraphs: SmallRye Fault Tolerance's @CircuitBreaker: five calls in the rolling window, all failed, open it for ten seconds, and two successful trial calls close it again. @CircuitBreakerName gives it the name that CircuitBreakerMaintenance reads for the breaker-state endpoint. @Fallback names a method that receives the cause, so the response says why it fell back: circuit_open when the breaker refused the call, upstream_<status> or upstream_unreachable when the call failed. One breaker per dependency.
